newsitem.title: USA: Atlanta mayor proposes $423.3 million budget.
newsitem.headline: Atlanta mayor proposes $423.3 million budget.

text.p: Mayor Bill Campbell has proposed a $423.3 million 1997 budget for the city of Atlanta, a decrease of $3.9 million or one percent from the previous year, city officials said Wednesday.
The budget for the calendar year is retroactive to Jan 1, but won't become final until approved by city commissioners late next month.
Sales tax has now surpassed property tax as the primary source of funding for city operations, according to the proposed budget.

"In 1996, sales tax grew to 19 percent of total revenue while property taxes, the most stable revenue source, decreased to 23 percent," Campbell said. "For 1997, it is estimated that sales taxes will represent 21.1 percent of total revenues while property taxes will decrease further to 17.3 percent."

The budget document said the $423.3 million general fund realized above normal growth in several revenue sources during 1996. Overall, revenues totaled $405.4 million, $17 million or 4.2 percent greater than the $388.8 million collected in 1995.

Revenue increases, some of which were attributed to the city hosting the Olympic Games, included $11.6 million in local option sales tax, $6 million in direct cost recovery from the Atlanta Committee for the Olympic Games, $5 million in insurance refunds, $2.5 million in vending concessions and $3.3 million in general businesses licenses.
The increases were partially offset by decreases in tangible and intangible property tax revenues of $15.6 million and $2.4 million, respectively.

The decrease in tangible property tax revenues was the result of an April 1996 court ruling that declared that the city's sharing of the local option sales tax with the Atlanta school system violated Georgia law.
The decrease in intangible property taxes occurred because the 1996 Georgia General Assembly discontinued the tax.
The budget anticipation rate for 1997 is 97.4 percent of the 1996 recurring revenues and is expected to produce $423.3 million, Campbell said.

He said the budget cuts spending by $34.9 million, but reinvests the savings in public safety, public works and parks. The cuts were made possible, in part, by the elimination of $8 million in Olympic-related expenses, $20 million in city support for the Atlanta Public Schools, and $1.2 million in overtime expenses.
Property tax revenue declined for the third consecutive year and will again decline slightly under the proposed budget.

The budget proposes creating a Revenue Collection Division for traffic court that would concentrate its efforts on collecting overdue fines. City officials said there is currently no provision to collect the $5.9 million that goes uncollected by the court each year.
